evidence.title: copilot-pull-request-reviewer on preppilot-backend/user-service/src/main/java/com/preppilot/userservice/config/JwtAuthFilter.java:46
evidence.text: Matching the raw request URI lets `/api/v1/%75sers/me/profile` skip this filter, although Spring MVC decodes it to the protected endpoint. SecurityConfig permits every request, so the controller can accept a caller-supplied X-User-Id and issue an access token for that user. Match the decoded, context-relative application path instead, and add an encoded-path regression test through the request-routing stack.

evidence.title: copilot-pull-request-reviewer on frontend/src/features/usage/useUsage.ts:7
evidence.text: Nothing refreshes usage when availableAt passes. On a Learn page left open and focused, MessageInput can remain disabled after the server allowance resets: isLocked checks time only during render, and query staleness alone does not trigger a refetch. The mock-interview start control has the same dependency. Schedule a refetch at the earliest availableAt so these controls recover without navigation or a reload.

evidence.title: copilot-pull-request-reviewer on frontend/src/features/usage/useUsage.ts:8
evidence.text: This shared query key survives logout: the app retains one QueryClient, while logout only clears Redux credentials. Another account can therefore see the previous account's usage and have actions disabled by its limits while the refetch is pending. Include the authenticated user ID in the key and disable the query without a user. Existing USAGE_QUERY_KEY prefix invalidations will still work.

evidence.title: copilot-pull-request-reviewer on preppilot-backend/topic-service/src/main/java/com/preppilot/topicservice/service/TopicService.java:34
evidence.text: The topic-limit check and insert are separate operations. A student with one topic can submit two concurrent requests with different names: both count one topic, pass the check, and save, exceeding the two-topic limit. The unique name index does not prevent this. Reserve capacity atomically per user in the database, coordinate it with creation and deletion, and release reservations when creation fails. A process-local lock would not protect multiple service instances.

evidence.title: copilot-pull-request-reviewer on preppilot-backend/topic-service/src/main/java/com/preppilot/topicservice/service/UsageLimitService.java:123
evidence.text: Refunding an earlier event does not restore a usable slot after a later event sets the lock. For example, two concurrent student tests consume both slots; the second succeeds and the first fails. The refund removes the first event, but remaining stays zero and new tests are rejected until the lock expires. Clear the lock atomically when the refunded event is actually present and removed, rather than only when it owns lockedBy. Repeated refunds must not clear a newer lock.
